title: Minimum Length of String After Deleting Similar Ends
constraints: s contains only the characters 'a', 'b' and 'c'
notes:
## Intuition

An operation is only possible when the first and last characters match, and then there is never a reason to hold back: taking the whole run of that character at each end removes the most and leaves ends that are at least as useful as any shorter cut. So the choice is forced, and the string shrinks greedily from both sides. Two indices, `left` and `right`, track what is left without building new strings. Trying every prefix and suffix length recursively also works, but is far slower.

## Approach

1. Put `left` at the first index and `right` at the last.
2. While `left < right` and `s[left] === s[right]`, call that shared character `ch`.
3. Move `left` forward past every `ch` (but not beyond `right`).
4. Move `right` backward past every `ch` (but not before `left`).
5. When the ends differ or meet, return `right - left + 1`, which is 0 when the pointers have crossed.

## Example 1, step by step

For `"ca"`, `left = 0` and `right = 1` point at `'c'` and `'a'`. They differ, so the loop never runs and the answer is `1 - 0 + 1 = 2`.

Example 3 shows the peeling: in `"aabccabba"` the ends are both `'a'`, so `left` skips to 2 and `right` to 7. Both are now `'b'`: `left` moves to 3 and `right` skips `"bb"` to 5. `s[3] = 'c'` and `s[5] = 'a'` differ, so the answer is `5 - 3 + 1 = 3`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): each index is passed by `left` or `right` at most once.
- Space: O(1): only two indices.

## Pitfalls

- A single remaining character cannot be removed, because the front and back blocks would share it; that is why the loop needs `left < right`.
- Once the ends match, a run may eat the whole middle (as in `"aaa"`); the bounds in the inner loops let the pointers cross and give length 0.
- Removing only one character from each side is not enough: in `"aabba"` that leaves `"abb"` and stops at 3, while removing the whole runs leaves `"bb"`, which then disappears.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `left` | index of the first character still in the string |
| `right` | index of the last character still in the string |
| `ch` | the character both ends share in the current operation |

narration.2: left marks the first character still kept.
narration.3: right marks the last character still kept.
narration.4: An operation is possible only when at least two characters remain and both ends match.
narration.6: Skip the whole run of it at the front...
narration.9: Then skip the run of it at the back, never passing left.
narration.13: The kept part runs from left to right; crossed pointers give 0.
